title: Exploring the Old Waterworks
transcript:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the old waterworks. This site supplied drinking water to the town for almost a century. Since the modern treatment plant opened upstream, the main buildings have become a small museum. We will visit the machinery hall first and then walk through the outdoor grounds.

Before we move, please check that you have a token for the audio guide. You collect the device at the desk inside the hall and return it at the end of the indoor visit. The guide is included in your ticket, but we use tokens to keep track of how many devices are out at one time.

The oldest surviving object is a large wooden pipe. It is displayed beside the entrance to the gallery, with a section removed so you can see its construction. Early visitors often assume that wood was only a temporary material. In fact, carefully maintained wooden pipes could remain in service for many years.

Beyond the pipe, you will find photographs showing how the town expanded around the waterworks. One sequence was taken from the same hillside at roughly ten-year intervals. Look particularly at the station in the background. Its growing platforms help us date photographs whose written labels were lost.

Our outdoor route follows a paved path around the former settling tanks. These are now shallow ponds, but please stay behind the low barriers. The edges can be slippery, and the plants growing over them hide changes in level. Anyone who prefers to avoid the walk can wait in the cafe, where a screen shows the main outdoor features.

You may notice that one pumping engine is missing a connecting rod. We have deliberately left the repair visible rather than making the machine look complete with a modern replacement. The missing section allows visitors to understand how the parts fitted together, and a diagram shows its original position.

The museum shop sells a booklet based on interviews with former employees. Their accounts include ordinary details, such as preparing lunch during a night shift, alongside descriptions of major breakdowns. We felt those everyday memories deserved space because machinery alone cannot explain what working here was like.

Please save general questions until we reach the courtyard. Inside the machinery hall, our group needs to keep moving so other visitors can pass. If you need assistance at any point, speak to me or to the volunteer wearing a green badge.

questions.prompt: Visitors exchange a ____ for an audio guide.
questions.explanation: 游客在大厅服务台用代币领取导览设备。

questions.prompt: The oldest surviving object on display is a wooden ____.
questions.explanation: 最古老的展品是一段木质水管。

questions.prompt: The growing platforms of the ____ help staff date old photographs.
questions.explanation: 远处车站站台的扩建有助于判断老照片年代。

questions.prompt: Why has the missing engine part not been replaced?
options: To show how the original mechanism fitted together
Because the museum cannot identify it
Because the engine will soon be removed
questions.answer: To show how the original mechanism fitted together
questions.explanation: 缺失处保留可让游客看清连接结构，并用图示补充。

questions.prompt: What is distinctive about the museum booklet?
options: It avoids accounts of mechanical failures
It includes everyday memories of workers
It was written when the waterworks first opened
questions.answer: It includes everyday memories of workers
questions.explanation: 册子同时收入夜班吃饭等日常回忆。
